headline._: Two outlets repeat one vendor report of 25 rooted servers; no primary statement is captured. Still no organisation confirms a compromise.
headline.exec: Nothing new that needs a decision. Still no organisation says it was hit.
headline.general: Nothing new for you. If someone runs your website, ask them if it is updated.
headline.security: Two outlets relay Dream Research's 25 rooted servers and say Unit 42 verified it; no Unit 42 or vendor statement is in the evidence, so it stays reported, not confirmed. Patch the PHP flaws as before.
headline.engineer: Nothing new to install. Confirm the fixed version is what is running.
headline.journalist: Two relays of one report are still one report. Keep "reported" apart from "confirmed hacked" until a primary is captured; the compromise stamps stay at 09:42 UTC.
headline.researcher: 715 sources by 17:13 UTC; 6 published today. Still wanted: Unit 42's brief of 29 October and any vendor advisory update.

items.text: A Japanese outlet (Innovatopia) relays that Palo Alto's Unit 42 independently verified Dream Research's report of 25 rooted servers. No Unit 42 or Palo Alto statement is in the evidence, so the newsroom keeps the report as reported, not confirmed, and does not name the affected vendor. Still no named organisation says it was compromised.
items.src: Innovatopia (30 October), read by the correspondent at 14:26 UTC; the journalist

items.text: A second outlet, Taiwan News, repeats the same Dream Research report and also names a vendor; both outlets draw on the one report. Neither is a primary statement, so the hold stands: reported, not confirmed, no product named on this site.
items.src: Taiwan News (30 October), read by the correspondent at 19:25 UTC; the journalist
